plans.note: No liability-cap heading surfaced in the outline; check the unnumbered body text after sec-p0001 and the Article 5 general provisions cluster (sec-5.4 is our only Article 5 anchor). Older intercompany/affiliate hosting agreements of this type often omit any cap or exclusion of consequential damages — if truly absent, treat as missing rather than deviation.

Search body text for indemnity language tied to Deerskin Products, site content and third-party IP claims arising from HDI's development/hosting. Note direction: HDI (host) should indemnify us; any indemnity we give for Deerskin Products content should be narrow. Likely absent given the short outline.

Presence rule — only flag if body text restricts the businesses the Company may operate or the products it may sell/source. Scan the Article 1 services/scope text around sec-1.4 for any covenant limiting our channels or product lines; nothing in the outline suggests one.

Presence rule — check whether Article 1 (scope of site development/hosting, sec-1.4 access provisions) makes HDI our sole/exclusive site developer or host, or requires that Deerskin Products be sold only through the HDI-hosted site. Flag only if the Company is bound; exclusivity running against HDI benefits us.

Direction rule — look for pricing/fee text obliging the Company to give HDI terms no worse than those given to other developers or hosts. An MFN in our favour is welcome and should not be flagged. No pricing section surfaced in the outline.

Presence rule — sec-5.4 appoints project managers/representatives on each side, which is where a personnel non-solicit is often lodged; read the surrounding Article 5 text for any hiring restriction on the Company, checking duration and a general-advertising carve-out.

The defined term "Termination Date" confirms a term/termination provision exists in body text not surfaced as a heading. Locate it and assess: whether the Company may terminate on notice without penalty, and whether HDI can walk away mid-term (asymmetry in HDI's favour is the deviation to watch).

Check the same term provision keyed to "Termination Date" for automatic renewal, the non-renewal notice window binding the Company, and any renewal price uplift. A missing uplift cap is a rationale note only, not a deviation.

Governing law/venue almost certainly sits in the Article 5 general provisions cluster near sec-5.4 (which also implies notices, given the "Time of Receipt" definition). Both parties are US direct-marketing entities, so New York or Delaware is likely and would be compliant; an accepted-but-not-preferred state is a rationale note.

Assignment/successors language should appear in the Article 5 miscellaneous run around sec-5.4. Confirm we may assign to affiliates and successors and that HDI has no termination or consent right on our change of control — relevant here given the affiliate relationship between the parties.

Direction rule — sec-1.4 (HDI providing the Company with access to the site) is the closest anchor for ownership of the site, code, look-and-feel, domain names, customer/order data and Deerskin Products content. We must own deliverables we pay for and all data we supply; any vesting of site IP or customer data in HDI is the deviation.

Read the access grant in sec-1.4 for scope: whether it extends to our affiliates and contractors, and whether HDI can revoke or suspend at will. If the document only grants access rather than a licence, assess this rule against that grant rather than marking it missing.

Look for HDI rights to inspect our usage, records or systems (frequency, notice, on-site access, cost allocation). Reporting/reconciliation duties tied to site sales are the likely vehicle; audits of HDI by us are in our favour and are not flagged.

Direction rule — check fee/performance text for stipulated sums, penalties or shortfall payments owed by the Company. Service credits or uptime credits flowing to us are beneficial and should not be redlined.

Search Article 1 services text for any HDI warranty on the development work and hosting availability, its duration and remedy, plus any "AS IS"/disclaimer that would negate it. Development-and-hosting agreements of this vintage frequently omit a performance warranty entirely.
No insurance heading in the outline; HDI hosts our site and handles customer/order data, so the rule applies. Scan the general provisions run around sec-5.4 before concluding it is missing.
Presence rule — look for minimum fee, minimum order-volume or take-or-pay commitments on the Company in the fee/services text, and whether any exit or true-up right accompanies them.

Check the provisions surrounding the "Termination Date" for wind-down duties: return or migration of site content, customer and order data, domain transfer and continued hosting during transition. Likely absent; if so, mark missing and request a transition-assistance and data-return clause.
